paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Moses is a hundred and twenty and he can't cross the Jordan, and he doesn't make it about himself. He tells the people, "The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you." (Deut 31:3) The leader changes, but the One going ahead of them stays the same.

That's why "Be strong and courageous" shows up again and again. Moses says it to the people and to Joshua, and then the LORD says it to Joshua too (Deut 31:6-8, 23). The reason is never that Joshua is tough. It's that "He will never leave you nor forsake you." (Deut 31:8) When your boss walks out the door and you're handed the keys, I'd be sweating like a cookie sheet straight out of the oven, so I need that promise too.

The other half is heavy, and I think it hurts. The LORD says the people will turn to other gods, and Moses says they're already rebellious (Deut 31:16, 27). So the law gets read aloud every seven years, the song gets taught, and the Book of the Law sits beside the ark (Deut 31:10-13, 19, 26). God knew their inclination before they ever entered the land (Deut 31:21), and He still went ahead of them, so don't hide your weak spots from Him. Keep His Word close and keep your apron on, because this story isn't over.
